findings.highlight: enjoying the spectacle
findings.evidenceJa: 廃墟を遊覧する
findings.governingReading: The sentence first describes touring the deserted ruins, then explicitly corrects who is enjoying them.
findings.explanation: The English prematurely inserts enjoyment into the activity before the narration’s correction.

findings.highlight: both still willing to fight
findings.evidenceJa: 健気にも未だ戦う意思を掲げる
findings.governingReading: The young pair admirably continue to uphold their will to fight.
findings.explanation: The English removes the valiant quality of their persistence.

findings.highlight: inhuman minds
findings.evidenceJa: 人でなくなったモノ
findings.governingReading: Only beings that are no longer human enjoy the devastation.
findings.explanation: The English changes dehumanized entities into an abstract class of minds.

findings.highlight: I left it alone for my good
findings.evidenceJa: 良かれと思い放任してきた
findings.governingReading: Zouken says he left the growth unchecked believing that doing so was for the best.
findings.explanation: The English makes the beneficiary explicitly himself and turns ostensible good judgment into self-interest.

findings.highlight: I may have to eliminate it soon
findings.evidenceJa: そろそろ刈り取らねばならぬ
findings.governingReading: Zouken suggests that it may be time to reap what he allowed to grow.
findings.explanation: The English removes the cultivation and harvest metaphor central to his manipulation.

findings.highlight: The old man laughs
findings.evidenceJa: 老人が嗤う
findings.governingReading: The old man gives a mocking or scornful laugh.
findings.explanation: The English removes the contempt encoded in the marked laugh verb.

findings.highlight: The man and the white skull roam
findings.evidenceJa: 白い髑髏を引き連れたソレは、闇に溶け込みながら
findings.governingReading: The old man, accompanied by the white skull, blends into the darkness as he roams.
findings.explanation: The English turns leader and follower into equal subjects and omits their blending into darkness.

findings.highlight: They are watching the girl and the boy
findings.evidenceJa: その視線の先には少年と少女がいた
findings.governingReading: The boy and girl lie at the end of the old man’s gaze.
findings.explanation: The English pluralizes the observer and attributes the watching to both figures.

findings.highlight: an enemy is an enemy, no matter how weak
findings.evidenceJa: どんなに小さかろうと障害は障害
findings.governingReading: For Assassin, an obstacle remains an obstacle however small it may be.
findings.explanation: The English changes obstacle size into enemy combat weakness.

findings.highlight: assassinate them if they are too strong to match
findings.evidenceJa: 手に負えないモノならなんであろうと排除する
findings.governingReading: Whatever cannot be kept under control is to be removed, regardless of what it is.
findings.explanation: The English narrows removal to assassination and recasts uncontrollability as superior combat strength.

findings.highlight: a rule he must obey
findings.evidenceJa: 徹守するべき不文律
findings.governingReading: This is an unwritten law Assassin must observe absolutely.
findings.explanation: The English omits both its unwritten nature and strictness.

findings.highlight: We can kill them here
findings.evidenceJa: この場で殺してもよいのでは
findings.governingReading: Assassin proposes to his master that they might kill the pair here.
findings.explanation: The English turns a deferential proposal into a statement of capability or permission.

findings.highlight: We let them live until now
findings.evidenceJa: ここまで生かしておいた
findings.governingReading: Zouken says he has deliberately kept them alive until this point.
findings.explanation: The English pluralizes the agency behind his long manipulation.

findings.highlight: This thing that wears human form
findings.evidenceJa: 齢五百を超える
findings.governingReading: The thing has lived beyond five hundred years and is rotten to the marrow.
findings.explanation: The English omits the five-century duration of Zouken’s corruption.

findings.highlight: ignored
findings.evidenceJa: 人の世に疎まれ
findings.governingReading: The sacrificial victim has been shunned and regarded with aversion by human society.
findings.explanation: The English weakens active social revulsion into being ignored.

findings.highlight: It tries to not hate the world as long as it has at least one ally on its side
findings.evidenceJa: その味方が住む世界を嫌わぬよう努めておる
findings.governingReading: The victim strives not to hate the world because her sole ally inhabits that world.
findings.explanation: The English omits the relationship that makes hatred of the world implicate the ally.

findings.highlight: love
findings.evidenceJa: 愛欲
findings.governingReading: Zouken mockingly calls the attachment affectionate or erotic desire.
findings.explanation: The English generalizes his deliberately charged term to love.

findings.highlight: no matter what happens to it
findings.evidenceJa: 何をされようと
findings.governingReading: The victim cannot fully hate humanity no matter what is done to her.
findings.explanation: The English removes the agents inflicting abuse and recasts it as impersonal events.

findings.highlight: he made it last so long
findings.evidenceJa: あそこまで保たせてくれた
findings.governingReading: Zouken credits the boy with sustaining the victim as far as this stage.
findings.explanation: The English turns progress to a designed breaking point into vague duration.

findings.highlight: The old man laughs
findings.evidenceJa: 呵々、と愉快げに老人は笑う
findings.governingReading: Zouken laughs loudly and delightedly, intoxicated by his own clever scheme.
findings.explanation: The English removes the laugh’s booming manner and his self-satisfied pleasure.

findings.highlight: like a white skull
findings.evidenceJa: 骨頭のようだった
findings.governingReading: The old man’s teeth sound like a bare skull rattling in the wind.
findings.explanation: The English adds “white,” needlessly inviting confusion with Assassin, the scene’s separately named white skull.
